questions.question_hindi:
निम्नलिखित अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) पर विचार कीजिए।
अभिकथन (A): अनुच्छेद 21क के अंतर्गत शिक्षा का मौलिक अधिकार अपने आप लागू हो जाता है और इसके लिए किसी कानून की आवश्यकता नहीं थी।
कारण (R): अनुच्छेद 21क कहता है कि राज्य निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा “ऐसे तरीके से, जैसा राज्य कानून द्वारा निर्धारित करे” उपलब्ध कराएगा; इसलिए RTE अधिनियम जैसे कार्यान्वयन कानून की आवश्यकता थी।
सही विकल्प चुनिए।
options_hindi: A और R दोनों सही हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है।
A और R दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
A सही है, लेकिन R गलत है।
A गलत है, लेकिन R सही है।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Fundamental Right to Education (Article 21A) is self-executing and did not require any legislation to be implemented.
Reason (R): Article 21A explicitly states that the State shall provide free and compulsory education "in such manner as the State may, by law, determine," which necessitated the enactment of the RTE Act.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Article 21A was not self-executing because its text explicitly specified that free and compulsory education would be provided "in such manner as the State may, by law, determine." Enacting enabling statutory legislation (the RTE Act, 2009) was required, rendering the assertion false while the reason correctly explains the text.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: A गलत है, लेकिन R सही है। अनुच्छेद 21क का पाठ कहता है कि राज्य छह से चौदह वर्ष तक के बच्चों को निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा ऐसे तरीके से उपलब्ध कराएगा जैसा कानून द्वारा निर्धारित हो। इस भाषा ने अधिकार के व्यावहारिक कार्यान्वयन के लिए विधायी ढाँचे की आवश्यकता स्पष्ट की। RTE अधिनियम, 2009 ने प्रवेश, उपस्थिति, पूर्णता, विद्यालयी जिम्मेदारियों और लागू मानकों से जुड़े प्रावधान प्रदान किए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) A is false but R is true

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 21A was not self-executing because its text explicitly specified that free and compulsory education would be provided "in such manner as the State may, by law, determine." Enacting enabling statutory legislation (the RTE Act, 2009) was required, rendering the assertion false while the reason correctly explains the text.

Assertion (A): Private unaided schools have the fundamental right to establish their own fee structure.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In TMA Pai Foundation (2002), the Supreme Court affirmed that private unaided educational institutions have autonomy to establish fee structures and generate reasonable surpluses for growth. questions.question_english: The Supreme Court judgment in the Environmental & Ecological Protection Committee v. State of Kerala emphasized environmental education. Which fundamental duty underscores the need for schools to teach environmental protection?
options_english: Article 51A(a)
Article 51A(c)
Article 51A(g)
Article 51A(j)
questions.explanation_english: Article 51A(g) explicitly mandates that every citizen of India has a fundamental duty to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures. This duty underpins compulsory environmental studies and conservation programs across school curricula.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: अनुच्छेद 51क(छ)। यह प्रत्येक नागरिक का कर्तव्य बताता है कि वह वनों, झीलों, नदियों और वन्यजीवों सहित प्राकृतिक पर्यावरण की रक्षा और सुधार करे तथा जीवधारियों के प्रति करुणा रखे। पर्यावरण शिक्षा विद्यार्थियों में इस कर्तव्य की समझ और व्यावहारिक जिम्मेदारी विकसित कर सकती है। अन्य विकल्प संविधान के आदर, राष्ट्रीय एकता या उत्कृष्टता जैसे अलग-अलग कर्तव्यों से संबंधित हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Article 51A(g)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 51A(g) explicitly mandates that every citizen of India has a fundamental duty to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures. This duty underpins compulsory environmental studies and conservation programs across school curricula.

questions.question_english: Which constitutional provision creates an obligation on the part of the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes?
options_english: Article 41
Article 45
Article 46

questions.explanation_english: Article 46 of the Directive Principles of State Policy directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, specifically highlighting Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. It also mandates protecting these groups from social injustice and all forms of exploitation across administrative domains.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर अनुच्छेद 46 है। यह राज्य के नीति-निदेशक तत्वों का हिस्सा है और राज्य को कमजोर वर्गों के शैक्षिक तथा आर्थिक हितों को विशेष देखभाल के साथ बढ़ावा देने का निर्देश देता है। इसमें विशेष रूप से अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों का उल्लेख है। यह अनुच्छेद समान अवसर और सामाजिक न्याय के उद्देश्य से शैक्षणिक सहायता तथा लक्षित उपायों के लिए संवैधानिक मार्गदर्शन देता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Article 46

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 46 of the Directive Principles of State Policy directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, specifically highlighting Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. It also mandates protecting these groups from social injustice and all forms of exploitation across administrative domains.

questions.question_hindi:
स्थिति पर विचार कीजिए।
केंद्र सरकार समग्र शिक्षा योजना शुरू करती है, जिसमें सर्व शिक्षा अभियान, RMSA और शिक्षक शिक्षा को समाहित किया गया है। योजना के लिए राज्यों को 40 प्रतिशत धन देना है। एक राज्य इसे अपनी स्वायत्तता में हस्तक्षेप बताते हुए मना कर देता है। शिक्षा के समवर्ती-सूची ढाँचे में ऐसी केंद्र प्रायोजित योजनाओं को संवैधानिक आधार किस प्रावधान से मिल सकता है?
options_hindi: अनुच्छेद 248 के अंतर्गत संसद की अनन्य अवशिष्ट विधायी शक्ति का सीधे उपयोग करके।
सार्वजनिक प्रयोजनों के लिए अनुदान देने की अनुच्छेद 282 की शक्ति का उपयोग करके।
अनुच्छेद 360 के अंतर्गत राष्ट्रीय वित्तीय आपातकाल घोषित करके।
संघ सूची की प्रविष्टि 66 के अंतर्गत उच्च शिक्षा के मानकों पर केंद्रीय विधायी अधिकार का उपयोग करके।

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english: Read the situation below and answer the question that follows: The Union Government launches the Samagra Shiksha scheme, subsuming SSA, RMSA, and TE. The scheme requires states to contribute 40% of the funds. A state refuses, citing it as an infringement on its autonomy. Under the Concurrent List framework, how are such Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) constitutionally justified in education?
options_english: By directly invoking the exclusive residuary legislative powers vested in the Parliament of India under Article 248.
By utilizing Article 282 to make grants for public financial purposes.
By issuing formal constitutional proclamations declaring a nationwide financial emergency under Article 360.
By exercising the Union's legislative authority over higher education standards under Entry 66 of List I.
questions.explanation_english: Article 282 empowers the Union or a State to make financial grants for any public purpose, even if outside their direct legislative domain. Centrally Sponsored Schemes like Samagra Shiksha are legally structured and funded under Article 282 grants, facilitating shared Centre-State financial participation in educational development.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: अनुच्छेद 282। यह संघ या राज्य को किसी सार्वजनिक प्रयोजन के लिए अनुदान देने की अनुमति देता है, भले ही वह प्रयोजन उनके प्रत्यक्ष विधायी क्षेत्र से बाहर हो। समग्र शिक्षा जैसी केंद्र प्रायोजित योजनाओं में वित्तीय सहायता तथा केंद्र-राज्य हिस्सेदारी की व्यवस्था इस तरह के सार्वजनिक-वित्तीय प्रावधानों से जुड़ सकती है। अनुच्छेद 248 अवशिष्ट विधायी शक्ति, अनुच्छेद 360 वित्तीय आपातकाल और संघ सूची की प्रविष्टि 66 उच्च शिक्षा के मानकों के समन्वय तथा निर्धारण से संबंधित है; ये दिए गए प्रसंग का सबसे सीधा आधार नहीं हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) By utilizing Article 282 to make grants for public financial purposes.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 282 empowers the Union or a State to make financial grants for any public purpose, even if outside their direct legislative domain. Centrally Sponsored Schemes like Samagra Shiksha are legally structured and funded under Article 282 grants, facilitating shared Centre-State financial participation in educational development.

questions.question_english: A state government decides to completely take over the management of all private unaided schools in the state, citing poor educational standards. This action would most likely be struck down by the courts as a violation of:
options_english: Article 14
Article 19(1)(g)
Article 21A
Article 30(2)
questions.explanation_english: Establishing and running private educational institutions is protected as an "occupation" under Article 19(1)(g). Completely nationalizing or taking over management of all private unaided schools without reasonable necessity constitutes an arbitrary, disproportionate restriction, violating freedom of occupation under Article 19(1)(g).
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: अनुच्छेद 19(1)(छ)। शैक्षणिक संस्था स्थापित करना और चलाना व्यवसाय/व्यवसायिक गतिविधि की स्वतंत्रता से जुड़ा है। राज्य शिक्षा के मानकों, सुरक्षा और सार्वजनिक हित के लिए उचित विनियमन कर सकता है, लेकिन सभी निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालयों का व्यापक और स्वतः प्रबंधन अधिग्रहण, बिना आवश्यक और आनुपातिक आधार के, इस स्वतंत्रता पर अत्यधिक प्रतिबंध हो सकता है। विशिष्ट संस्था के विरुद्ध उचित निरीक्षण या सुधारात्मक कार्रवाई और सभी संस्थाओं का सामूहिक अधिग्रहण अलग-अलग स्थितियाँ हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Article 19(1)(g)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Establishing and running private educational institutions is protected as an "occupation" under Article 19(1)(g). Completely nationalizing or taking over management of all private unaided schools without reasonable necessity constitutes an arbitrary, disproportionate restriction, violating freedom of occupation under Article 19(1)(g).

questions.question_english:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Minority educational institutions have the absolute right to appoint any person as a teacher, regardless of their academic qualifications.
Reason (R): The State cannot impose regulations prescribing minimum educational qualifications for teachers in minority institutions, as it would violate Article 30(1).
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: The assertion is false because minority institutions do not possess absolute authority to appoint unqualified teachers. Reason R is true in recognizing that while Article 30(1) protects management choice, the State retains authority to enforce minimum qualification standards and academic credentials for teaching positions.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: A गलत है, लेकिन R सही है। अल्पसंख्यक संस्थानों को अपने शिक्षकों और प्रबंधन के चयन में स्वायत्तता प्राप्त है, पर यह अयोग्य शिक्षकों की नियुक्ति का निरपेक्ष अधिकार नहीं है। राज्य शैक्षणिक मानक, न्यूनतम योग्यता और शिक्षण की गुणवत्ता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए उचित नियम बना सकता है। अनुच्छेद 30(1) संस्थान के अल्पसंख्यक चरित्र और प्रशासन की स्वतंत्रता की रक्षा करता है, लेकिन हर शैक्षणिक विनियमन को निषिद्ध नहीं करता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) A is false but R is true

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The assertion is false because minority institutions do not possess absolute authority to appoint unqualified teachers. Reason R is true in recognizing that while Article 30(1) protects management choice, the State retains authority to enforce minimum qualification standards and academic credentials for teaching positions.

questions.question_english: Article 30(1) of the Constitution grants the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice to:
options_english: Religious minorities recognized under central or state minority declarations only.
All religious or linguistic minorities.
Linguistic minorities maintaining a distinct language or script within the region.
Any socially and educationally backward class identified by the state commissions.
questions.explanation_english: Article 30(1) grants all religious and linguistic minorities the fundamental right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. This constitutional protection applies equally across the territory of India to both religious and linguistic minority groups, ensuring they can preserve their unique identity and impart education to their community while maintaining operational and administrative autonomy in running their institutions.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B है। अनुच्छेद 30(1) धार्मिक और भाषाई दोनों प्रकार के अल्पसंख्यकों को अपनी पसंद के शैक्षणिक संस्थान स्थापित करने तथा उनका प्रशासन करने का मौलिक अधिकार देता है। इस अधिकार का उद्देश्य अल्पसंख्यकों की शैक्षणिक और सांस्कृतिक पहचान की रक्षा करना है। यह अधिकार राज्य के सभी वैध नियामक मानकों से पूर्ण छूट नहीं देता, लेकिन संस्थान की अल्पसंख्यक पहचान और प्रशासनिक स्वायत्तता की रक्षा करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) All religious or linguistic minorities.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 30(1) grants all religious and linguistic minorities the fundamental right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. This constitutional protection applies equally across the territory of India to both religious and linguistic minority groups, ensuring they can preserve their unique identity and impart education to their community while maintaining operational and administrative autonomy in running their institutions.

questions.question_english: The fundamental duty prescribed under Article 51A(k) was added to the Constitution on the recommendation of which of the following?
options_english: Recommendations submitted by the Swaran Singh Committee on fundamental duties.
Detailed financial recommendations outlined by the Tapas Majumdar Committee.
Direct addition via the 86th Amendment Act without a specific committee.
Institutional center-state relations recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission.
questions.explanation_english: The fundamental duty under Article 51A(k)— requiring parents or guardians to provide education opportunities to children aged six to fourteen—was added directly by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act in 2002 alongside Article 21A. While Swaran Singh Committee recommended initial duties in 1976, clause (k) was added later via the 86th Amendment.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर C है। अनुच्छेद 51क(क) माता-पिता या अभिभावकों का यह मौलिक कर्तव्य निर्धारित करता है कि वे 6 से 14 वर्ष के अपने बच्चे या प्रतिपाल्य को शिक्षा के अवसर दें। यह प्रावधान 86वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2002 द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। स्रोत की उत्तर-व्याख्या के अनुसार इसे तपस मजूमदार समिति की वित्तीय सिफारिशों या सरकारिया आयोग की रिपोर्ट से नहीं जोड़ा गया है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Direct addition via the 86th Amendment Act without a specific committee.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The fundamental duty under Article 51A(k)— requiring parents or guardians to provide education opportunities to children aged six to fourteen—was added directly by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act in 2002 alongside Article 21A. While Swaran Singh Committee recommended initial duties in 1976, clause (k) was added later via the 86th Amendment.

options_english: All students enrolled across all institutions must achieve identical academic scores in examinations.
Equals must be treated equally, allowing reasonable classification for disadvantaged groups.
The state administration must treat all individual students identically regardless of their personal socio-economic circumstances.
Private educational institutions are completely prohibited from operating within the territory of India under any circumstances.
questions.explanation_english: Equality before the law under Article 14 does not mean uniform treatment of unequals. It permits reasonable classification based on intelligible differentia having a rational relation to the objective sought. In education, this allows affirmative policies, scholarships, and targeted quotas to support socio-economically disadvantaged students.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: समान स्थिति वाले व्यक्तियों के साथ समान व्यवहार, और वंचित समूहों के लिए तर्कसंगत वर्गीकरण की अनुमति। अनुच्छेद 14 का समानता सिद्धांत हर व्यक्ति के साथ परिस्थितियों की परवाह किए बिना यांत्रिक रूप से एक जैसा व्यवहार करने की माँग नहीं करता। उचित उद्देश्य और तर्कसंगत आधार पर वर्गीकरण की अनुमति है, जैसे वंचित समूहों के लिए विशेष शैक्षणिक सहायता। इसका उद्देश्य मनमानी रोकना और वास्तविक समानता को बढ़ावा देना है, न कि सभी विद्यार्थियों के परिणामों को समान बनाना।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Equals must be treated equally, allowing reasonable classification for disadvantaged groups.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Equality before the law under Article 14 does not mean uniform treatment of unequals. It permits reasonable classification based on intelligible differentia having a rational relation to the objective sought. In education, this allows affirmative policies, scholarships, and targeted quotas to support socio-economically disadvantaged students.

questions.question_english: A Principal wants to deny admission to a transgender child in a regular government school, suggesting they attend a "special school". Under the NALSA v. Union of India judgment, read with constitutional provisions, this action:
options_english: Is legally valid because constitutional protections under Article 21A apply strictly to male and female children.
Violates Articles 14, 15, and 21 guarantees of equal rights and non-discrimination.
Is legally valid under the administrative doctrine of reasonable classification for specialized educational institutions.
Violates cultural rights guaranteed under Article 29, but does not constitute discrimination under Article 15.
questions.explanation_english: In NALSA v. Union of India (2014), the Supreme Court recognized transgender persons as a third gender, holding that equality (Article 14), nondiscrimination on grounds of sex/gender (Article 15), and personal dignity (Article 21) protect them. Denying regular school inclusion violates these fundamental rights.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: यह अनुच्छेद 14, 15 और 21 के तहत समानता और गैर-भेदभाव के अधिकारों का उल्लंघन है। NALSA बनाम भारत संघ (2014) मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने ट्रांसजेंडर व्यक्तियों की लैंगिक पहचान को मान्यता दी और उनके लिए समानता तथा गरिमा के संवैधानिक संरक्षण को स्पष्ट किया। बच्चे को केवल लैंगिक पहचान के कारण नियमित विद्यालय से बाहर करना भेदभावपूर्ण है। समावेशी प्रवेश नीति में सभी बच्चों को समान अवसर मिलना चाहिए, जब तक किसी विशेष आवश्यकता के लिए बच्चे और परिवार की सहमति तथा वैध आधार पर उपयुक्त व्यवस्था न की जाए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Violates Articles 14, 15, and 21 guarantees of equal rights and non-discrimination.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In NALSA v. Union of India (2014), the Supreme Court recognized transgender persons as a third gender, holding that equality (Article 14), nondiscrimination on grounds of sex/gender (Article 15), and personal dignity (Article 21) protect them. Denying regular school inclusion violates these fundamental rights.

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the constitutional position of linguistic minorities:
I. Article 29 grants linguistic minorities the right to conserve their language.
II. Article 30 grants them the right to establish and administer educational institutions.
III. Article 350A provides a fundamental right to be taught in the mother tongue at the higher secondary stage. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
options_english: I and II
I and III
II and III
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Article 29 protects cultural conservation, and Article 30 grants minorities the right to establish and manage educational institutions. Statement III is incorrect because Article 350A is a directive (not a fundamental right) encouraging primary (not higher secondary) instruction in the mother tongue.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I और II। अनुच्छेद 29(1) विशिष्ट भाषा, लिपि या संस्कृति वाले नागरिकों के किसी भी वर्ग को उसे सुरक्षित रखने का अधिकार देता है। अनुच्छेद 30(1) धार्मिक और भाषाई अल्पसंख्यकों को शैक्षणिक संस्थान स्थापित करने और उनका प्रशासन करने का अधिकार देता है। तीसरा कथन गलत है: अनुच्छेद 350क प्राथमिक स्तर पर भाषाई अल्पसंख्यक बच्चों को मातृभाषा में शिक्षा की सुविधाएँ उपलब्ध कराने का प्रयास करने का निर्देश देता है; यह उच्च माध्यमिक स्तर के लिए मौलिक अधिकार नहीं है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 29 protects cultural conservation, and Article 30 grants minorities the right to establish and manage educational institutions. Statement III is incorrect because Article 350A is a directive (not a fundamental right) encouraging primary (not higher secondary) instruction in the mother tongue.

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the 'Doctrine of Pith and Substance' in educational legislation:
I. It is used to determine the true nature and character of a legislation to check if it falls within the legislative competence of the Union or the State.
II. If a State Education Act incidentally touches upon a Central subject but in 'pith and substance' relates to education (Concurrent List), it is valid.
III. It strictly prohibits the Union from making any laws on education. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
options_english: I and II
II and III
I and III
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: The Doctrine of Pith and Substance assesses the true nature of legislation to resolve jurisdictional overlaps between Union and State Lists. Statement III is incorrect because the doctrine does not prohibit Parliamentary legislation on education; rather, it validates laws whose primary substance falls within competent legislative domain.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I और II। पिथ एंड सब्स्टेंस सिद्धांत कानून के वास्तविक विषय और उद्देश्य की जाँच करता है ताकि यह तय किया जा सके कि विधायिका अपने संवैधानिक क्षेत्र में काम कर रही थी या नहीं। यदि कानून का सार उसके विधायी क्षेत्र में आता है, तो किसी दूसरे क्षेत्र को आकस्मिक रूप से छूना उसे स्वतः अमान्य नहीं करता। तीसरा कथन गलत है, क्योंकि शिक्षा समवर्ती सूची में है और संसद को भी इस विषय पर कानून बनाने की विधायी क्षमता प्राप्त है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Doctrine of Pith and Substance assesses the true nature of legislation to resolve jurisdictional overlaps between Union and State Lists. Statement III is incorrect because the doctrine does not prohibit Parliamentary legislation on education; rather, it validates laws whose primary substance falls within competent legislative domain.

Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Constitution of India uses the word "minorities" but does not define it.
Reason (R): The definition of minorities was explicitly left to the respective State legislatures to define in the State List.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

questions.explanation_english: The Constitution mentions minorities in Articles 29 and 30 but does not define the term anywhere. The reason is false because the definition was not delegated to State List legislation; rather, judicial decisions established that minority status is determined at the State level based on demographic population data.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) A is true but R is false

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Constitution mentions minorities in Articles 29 and 30 but does not define the term anywhere. The reason is false because the definition was not delegated to State List legislation; rather, judicial decisions established that minority status is determined at the State level based on demographic population data.
